For MobileViT-S, APTOS class-wise recalls for grades 0-4 were 97.0%, 68.9%, 83.0%, 35.9%, and 62.7%; the corresponding MESSIDOR-2 recalls were 89.5%, 16.7%, 24.2%, 12.0%, and 37.1%. On MESSIDOR-2, 214/270 Mild DR images (79.3%) were predicted as No DR and 54/75 Severe DR images (72.0%) as Moderate DR. Referable-DR prevalence versus mean predicted risk was 40.65% versus 39.06% on APTOS and 26.20% versus 15.74% on MESSIDOR-2. External Brier score was 0.1364 (95% CI 0.1204-0.1527), ECE 0.1051 (0.0858-0.1265), calibration intercept 1.43 (1.20-1.65), and slope 0.69 (0.62-0.79), indicating systematic underestimation and overly dispersed predictions. Figure 2 and Table S3 summarize this post hoc exploratory analysis.

TFLite Verification and Inference-Only Benchmarking. For each model, PyTorch and TFLite top-1 predictions agreed for 50/50 real images and 10/10 seeded random tensors. Across the real images, mean absolute logit differences ranged from 1.71 × 10⁻⁶ to 1.40 × 10⁻⁵, and maximum absolute differences ranged from 8.58 × 10⁻⁶ to 8.96 × 10⁻⁵; all were below the 1 × 10⁻³ tolerance. These results support numerical fidelity on the evaluated inputs but do not demonstrate equivalence for all possible inputs. On the single benchmark device, MobileNetV3-Large had the lowest measured mean latency, EfficientNet-Lite0 had the smallest model file, and ResNet-50 had the largest file and highest measured latency. The device was a Huawei DBR-W00 running Android 12 on a Snapdragon 865-class platform.
